summary: This is a careful, fully preregistered, and well‑archived paired NetOps experiment whose execution and analysis artifacts are reproducible. The study produced a degenerate ceiling outcome (200/200 SAFE) under the executed shared‑generation semantics; the manuscript transparently reports that the preregistered causal hypothesis was not testable and provides an artifact‑grounded diagnosis and recommendations. The underlying execution, scoring, and analysis appear sound. However, required presentation revisions from the prior review remain: the manuscript still reads like an artifact inventory (metadata‑heavy), uses raw provenance/URL fragments instead of conventional scholarly citations, and contains manifest/path/sha enumerations in the main narrative rather than concise archival pointers. These defects impair readability and cause the submission to read like an artifact report rather than a focused conference short paper.
critical_issues: Main narrative remains metadata‑heavy and manifest‑focused, with long lists of artifact paths/SHAs embedded in the body rather than referred to concisely; this makes the paper read like an artifact report instead of a conference paper focused on scientific interpretation (presentation defect).

Related Work and in‑text citations still appear as raw URLs or provenance fragments rather than normal bibliographic citations (author/year/venue) tied to the verified bibliography; this reduces scholarly readability and prevents proper literature grounding.

Several paragraphs present provenance lists where concise scholarly prose should summarize the evidence and point to the archive; the manuscript therefore fails the prior required change to compress provenance bookkeeping into a short archival pointer and move details to the Disclosure/compact appendix within the same five pages.
required_revisions: Compress and de‑emphasize manifest/path/SHA listings in the main text: replace long path lists with concise referential wording (e.g., “full execution and analysis artifacts are archived in the supplied bundle; representative identifiers appear in the Disclosure”) and move full manifest details to the Disclosure or a single compact appendix subsection within the five pages. (Resolvable from supplied artifacts.)

Replace inline raw URLs/provenance fragments used as citations with conventional bibliographic citations (author, year, venue) drawn from the verified bibliography record; ensure each narrative citation matches an entry in the archived BibTeX/verified bibliography. (Resolvable from supplied artifacts.)

Rewrite the metadata‑heavy paragraphs identified in Related Work/Methods/Results (total ≤~200 words) into normal scholarly prose that: (a) summarizes provenance succinctly with a single archival pointer, (b) focuses discussion on scientific interpretation and implications rather than enumerating artifacts, and (c) preserves reproducibility by referring readers to the archived manifest for details. Provide the revised text in the manuscript body. (Resolvable from supplied artifacts.)
optional_revisions: Shorten Related Work to the 3–5 closest methodological/empirical items and move peripheral citations to the references only to improve information density (use the verified bibliography).

Add a compact one‑row table or compact figure that summarizes key resource trade‑offs (model_calls_used vs planned_model_calls; N tasks; generation semantics used) using numbers from execution_manifest.json to help readers — keep it very compact to preserve the five‑page limit.

If space permits, add a single concise sentence clarifying repair status (e.g., “the guarded pipeline could invoke repairs but repair_provider_trace entries are null for confirmatory episodes, so no repairs were applied”), or move that clarification to the Methods paragraph for clarity.
